questions.question: What is the term for a dome-shaped monument that contains sacred relics in Buddhism?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Stupa**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• A **Stupa** is a dome-shaped architectural structure that serves as a sacred monument in Buddhism, often housing relics of the Buddha or other significant monks.
 
• It symbolizes the **enlightened mind** and the path to enlightenment in Buddhist philosophy.
 
• Stupas are typically surrounded by a **circumambulatory path** where devotees walk in a clockwise direction as an act of devotion.
 
• Some of the most famous stupas include the **Sanchi Stupa** in India, the Great Stupa at Borobudur in Indonesia, and the Boudhanath Stupa in Nepal.
 
• Stupas are often adorned with **ornamental gateways (toranas)** and inscriptions that depict Buddhist teachings and historical events.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Vihar**: Refers to a Buddhist monastery or residence for monks and nuns, often used as a place for meditation and learning.
 
• **Chaitya**: A prayer hall or shrine in Buddhism, often containing a stupa and used for congregational worship.
 
• **Stambha**: A free-standing pillar, often inscribed with edicts or symbols of Buddhist philosophy, such as the Ashokan Pillars.
 
• **Relics in Stupas**: These may include physical remains of the Buddha, such as ashes or bones, as well as objects associated with him, like sacred texts or robes.
 
• **Symbolism of the Stupa**: The dome represents the universe, the square base symbolizes the earth, and the spire signifies spiritual ascent or enlightenment.

questions.question: How many Mahajanapadas were there during the age of Buddha?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**16**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• During the lifetime of Lord Gautam Buddha, 16 great powers (Mahajanpadas) existed in the 7th and early 6th centuries BC.
 
• These were Kasi, Kosala, Anga, Magadha, Vajji, Malla, Chedi, Vatsa, Kuru, Panchala, Machcha, Surasena, Assaka, Avanti, Gandhara and Kamboja.​

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Buddha was born in BC 563 in Lumbini (near the Indo-Nepal Border) and died at the age of eighty in BC 483 at Kushinagar in UP.
 
• At the age of 29, Gautama left home and rejected his life of riches and embraced a lifestyle of asceticism.
 
• After 49 consecutive days of meditation, Gautama attained enlightenment under a pipal tree (Bodhi Tree) at Bodhgaya a village in Bihar.
 
• Buddha gave his first sermon in the village of Sarnath in UP. This event is known as Dharma-Chakra-Pravartana.

 
• **Buddhist Councils marked important turning points in early Buddhism, In total, 4 major Buddhist councils were convened-** 

 
 
• The First Council was held soon after the Mahaparinirvan of the Buddha, around 483 BC in the Sattapani cave at Rajgriha. 
 
• The second Council was held in 383 BC in Vaishali.
 
• The third council was held in 250 BC in Patliputra.
 
• The fourth Council was held in 1st century AD at Kundalvana, Kashmir.

• Pulakesi II reigned over the Chalukyas of Badami, an Indian royal dynasty that ruled large parts of southern and central India between the sixth and the twelfth centuries.

• Aparajita Varman was the last ruler of the Pallava dynasty.

questions.question: Harshvardhan's ambitions of extending his power to Deccan and South India were stopped by:
questions.solution:

__

• Harshavardhana, the ruler of North India, attempted to expand his influence to the Deccan and South India.
 
• Pulakesin II decisively defeated Harshavardhana near the banks of the river Narmada around 618-619 AD, halting his southern expansion.
 
• This victory is recorded in the Aihole inscription, composed by Pulakesin II's court poet, Ravikirti.
 
• The defeat of Harshavardhana by Pulakesin II is considered a significant event in Indian history as it marked the limit of Harshavardhana's territorial expansion.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• He established his capital at Kannauj and was known for his patronage of arts and literature.
 
• Harsha's reign is well-documented by the Chinese traveler Xuanzang (Hiuen Tsang).
 
 
 
• **Chalukya Dynasty**
 
 
• The Chalukya dynasty was an important South Indian dynasty that ruled large parts of southern and central India between the 6th and 12th centuries.
 
• Pulakesin II was one of the most notable rulers of the Chalukya dynasty.
 
 
 
• **Aihole Inscription**

questions.question: The famous source of Gupta empire, the Prayaga Prashasti is also known as the _____.

• **Samudra Gupta** court poet and minister **Harisena **composed the Allahabad pillar Inscription also known as Prayag Prasasti.
 
• The Pillar was an Ashokan Pillar erected by Asoka six centuries before him.
 
• This Inscription is a eulogy of Samudra Gupta and mentions the conquests of Samudra Gupta and the boundaries of the Gupta Empire.
 
• As per this inscription, Samudra Gupta defeated 9 kings in the North, and 12 Kings in the South, reducing all the Atavika states to vassalage.

• The Allahabad Prasasti was originally engraved on the Ashokan Pillar in Kausambhi near Allahabad.
 
• Later it was moved to the Allahabad fort.

questions.question: ______’s foster mother Mahapajapati Gotami was the first woman to be ordained as a bhikkhuni.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Buddha**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Buddha****’s foster mother Mahapajapati Gotami was the first woman to be ordained as a bhikkhuni**.
 
• **Mahapajapati Gotami** was the foster-mother, step-mother, and maternal aunt (mother's sister) of the Buddha.
 
 
• In the Buddhist tradition, she was the first woman to seek ordination for women, which she did from Gautama Buddha directly, and she became the first bhikkhuni (Buddhist nun).
 
• Tradition says Maya and Mahapajapati Gotami were Koliyan princess and **sisters of Suppabuddha**.
 
• Mahapajapati was both the Buddha's maternal aunt and adoptive mother, raising him after her sister Maya, the Buddha's birth mother died.
 
• She was considered the kindest mother who raised Siddhartha as her own child.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Bindusara**, also **Amitraghata or Amitrakhada or Amitrochates** was the second Mauryan emperor of India.

 
 
• He was the son of the dynasty's founder Chandragupta and the father of its most famous ruler Ashoka. 
 
 
 
• **Ashoka**, also known as Ashoka the Great, was an Indian emperor of the Maurya Dynasty, son of Bindusara, who ruled almost all of the Indian subcontinent from c. 268 to 232 BCE.

• **Kanchipuram** served as the capital of the Pallava Dynasty, which ruled parts of South India from the 3rd to 9th centuries CE.

• They were contemporaries of other prominent dynasties like the Chalukyas and Pandyas.
 
• Their reign marked the transition from **rock-cut architecture to structural temples**, influencing later dynasties such as the Cholas.

• The city is famous for **Kanchipuram silk sarees**, which are a significant cultural legacy.

• Later, they transitioned to structural temples made of stone, such as the **Kailasanatha Temple** in Kanchipuram.
 
• The Shore Temple at Mahabalipuram, built during Pallava rule, is a UNESCO World Heritage site.
 
• Their architectural innovations set the foundation for Dravidian temple architecture in South India.
 
 
 
• **Historical Significance**
 
 
• The Pallavas were instrumental in spreading Indian culture and religion to Southeast Asia through maritime trade and cultural exchanges.
 
• Their inscriptions, written in both Tamil and Sanskrit, provide valuable insights into the political and cultural history of ancient South India.
 
• Their governance and cultural achievements laid the groundwork for subsequent South Indian dynasties, such as the Cholas.
 
• Their advancements in art and architecture had a lasting impact on the cultural landscape of India and beyond.

• It was authored by the ancient Tamil scholar **Tolkappiyar**.
 
• This work is a comprehensive treatise on Tamil grammar, phonology, morphology, and syntax.
 
• **Tolkappiyam** also provides valuable insights into the social and cultural life of ancient Tamil society.

• **Ettutogai**

 
 
• Ettutogai, also known as the Eight Anthologies, is a classical Tamil poetic work.
 
• It is a collection of eight different anthologies of Tamil poems.
 
• These poems focus on various themes such as love, valor, and ethics, reflecting the Tamil culture and traditions.
 
 
 
• **Kalittogai**
 
 
• Kalittogai is a classical Tamil poetic work and one of the Eight Anthologies (Ettutogai).
 
• It comprises 150 poems focusing on the theme of love.
 
• The poems in Kalittogai are unique in their meter and style, known as Kali meter.
 
 
 
• **Narrinai**
 
 
• Narrinai is also part of the Eight Anthologies (Ettutogai).
 
• This work consists of 400 poems, primarily focusing on the theme of love.
 
• Narrinai poems are known for their simplicity and emotional depth.
